page: Microsoft Azure HC44-16rs is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the HCS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8168 processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes support for AVX, AVX-512f, AES, and FMA instructions. This server is equipped with 352.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 22.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of 717 GB, and the instance is both RDMA and Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the HC44-16rs demonstrates average performance across most standard compute and memory tasks. The Geekbench single-core score is 1170.0, while the multi-core score reaches 9639.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1631.16 GB/sec, which drops to 164.07 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database operations are supported by a Redis SET throughput of 26.41 million operations per second and a Passmark database score of 10797.1.

A key tradeoff of this configuration is its performance in sequential and AI-related tasks. Single-threaded gzip compression is weak at 23.76 GB/sec, and LLM inference speeds are limited, with a medium 7B model achieving only 7.44 tokens/sec for text generation and a large 70B model dropping to 4.52 tokens/sec for prompt processing. Given the high memory capacity, dedicated cores, and RDMA capabilities, this server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, and high-performance computing node configurations, rather than modern machine learning inference.
